rubric: Five equally weighted criteria, 0-2 each. Scores select only among browser-qualified configurations; otherwise they describe the preferred baseline for further investigation.

domainReuse.evidence: Native cached active query calls the shared complete(payload, resources) function; common fixture, commits, transactions and correctness oracle are reused unchanged.

typeSafety.evidence: World<Entity> and component-key operations retain the ordinary typed record shape. Public transport remains plain and independent of ECS handles.

lifecycleMutation.evidence: Explicit add/removeComponent, world.remove and world.clear suffice for the candidate layer. The shared worker coordinator handles generations, credits, cancellation and teardown.

captureProjection.evidence: Plain record values feed shared detached projection/capture directly; stable game IDs remain separate from object identity. Nested dirty tracking and predicate reindexing remain explicit.

packageIntegration.evidence: Pinned exports work through Vite and the Angular production packaging probe. The small implementation is inspectable, but sparse release cadence and transitive eventery CommonJS optimization warnings remain integration risks.

domainReuse.evidence: Native query reads the per-world payload and Float64 stores, calls the same complete(payload, resources) function, and reuses common fixture, commits, transactions and oracle.

typeSafety.evidence: Strict TypeScript passes, but query membership requires payload non-null assertions and does not establish every indexed-store access to the compiler.

lifecycleMutation.evidence: Candidate code owns numeric capacity growth/copying, recycled-handle cleanup, payload clearing, component membership and deleteWorld. These obligations remain inside one worker.

captureProjection.evidence: Projection/capture reconstruct records from game ordinal to ECS handle, payload array and separate numeric stores; restoration reverses that mapping. No handles cross the transport boundary.

packageIntegration.evidence: Pinned 0.4.0 exports and no runtime dependencies simplify packaging, while its version-specific storage/query API and project-owned capacity policy require ongoing care. Future shared numeric facilities are assessed separately and earn no speculative bonus here.

futureThreading: bitECS provides the more direct shared numeric store/query-buffer starting point. Neither provides an automatic parallel scheduler; actual parallel scalability is unmeasured.
